content.comment_body: Great, this works as I wanted! Thanks! Now I'd like to apply the same approach to another input. I duplicate the two logic blocks, set "1" in one variable and "0" in the other, and add a new variable in the memory configuration. For Master 2 configured as client, I add a network input at address VB: 2, but it doesn't function as expected—it was too simple! Does your method support only one input, or is there another way to configure this?
I previously wrote: If you plan to transfer multiple digital signals between [product_name] devices, you'll need a different approach. I developed a solution a while back—I'll look for it again.

Thanks for your time and for adapting my program. I appreciate your 15-bit example, but I'm not sure how to apply it to my use case. I don't see how to match it to my client setup, but I'll try to understand how it works.
I've included my custom function blocks into your program (server side).
Thanks! What I wanted to clarify is: how do I know which port to connect, say, I6 so it controls Q2 (likewise, I5 to Q3, I1 to Q15, and so on) on Master_2? I'll step back now—promise.
Why—was my support insufficient? I've attached an example for you to test and learn from.

Great, I think I understand now! Previously, I didn't realize that the blue annotation meant: I1 : 21 . 0. For Master 2, I had to enter NI1 (VB: 21, bit: 0) to match, and that works—thanks a lot! PS: I still don't get why, when the mapping address is 20, it also works for I1 : 21 . x, but since it works, that's fine.
And if I want client-to-server communication, is it possible with the same program?
In principle, yes. You'll need to use a different word in the variable memory area.
Here's another example to clarify further. The server transmits 15 bits to the client (VW20) and receives 15 bits from the client (VW30).

Thanks! One last question: you use addresses 20 and 30. How many addresses can I use? I'm just curious—is it possible to send (master 1 to master 2) 15 bits on address 20, 15 bits on address 30, 15 bits on address 40, etc.?

Like the famous saying: Yes, you can. You may use the two custom function blocks multiple times in your program—as long as there are enough available blocks. Addressing is flexible but always uses a word (2 bytes), so you can address at intervals of 2: 0, 2, 4, 6, and so forth.
Alright, thanks again for your help!

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered difficulties exchanging multiple digital signals between [product_name] devices, especially when mapping multiple inputs/outputs and configuring variable memory. There was confusion about extending solutions beyond one input, and example programs helped, but uncertainties persisted regarding address mapping and bidirectional data exchange. Users expressed wanting clearer guidance for handling these advanced data communication tasks.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek a simple, scalable method for configuring multiple digital exchanges between [product_name] devices. They expect clear directions or documentation for correct signal mapping and want clarity on enabling bidirectional communications using unified configurations.
